chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Abu Amara Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah saying:
If only two people remained on the earth, the second of them would be the Hujjah (Proof/Imam).

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْحُجَّةَ: The Hujjah (Proof/Imam), a title for the Imam who serves as the divine proof for humanity.
key_terms.فِي الْأَرْضِ: On the earth, referring to the global scope of the Imam's presence.

ai.seo_question: Who is the Hujjah if only two people remain on Earth?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the theological certainty of the Imam's presence (*Hujjiyyah*) regardless of the population size, a key concept in Shia eschatology regarding the final Imam. It highlights that the Imam's authority is intrinsic and not dependent on widespread recognition or numerical majority, ensuring the continuity of divine guidance until the Day of Judgment. This aligns with the Shia belief in the infallible Imam as the necessary link between God and humanity, even in times of obscurity (*Ghaybah*). Additional Quranic references: 2:124, 36:12. }

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (1) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah narrated from Muhammad bin Ja’far al-Qarashi from Muhammad bin al-Hasan bin Abul-Khattab from Muhammad bin Sinan that Abu Imara Hamza at-Tayyar had heard Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) saying: “
If there are no people on the earth except two men, one of them must be al-Hujjah (Imam al-Mahdi).”
